newsitem.title: USA: Exide seen rejecting Danaher bid.
newsitem.headline: Exide seen rejecting Danaher bid.

text.p: Exide Electronics Group Inc is expected to reject Danaher Corp's $20-per-share unsolicited takeover bid within the next 24 hours, sources close to the situation said.

Exide will likely announce a rejection of the offer either after Monday's market close or on Tuesday, and will not address other defensive moves, including possible discovery of a "white knight" friendly merger partner, one source said.
Spokesmen for both companies were not immediately available to comment.
Danaher announced its tender offer for Exide, a Raleigh, N.C.-based maker of uninterruptable power supply systems and software, on July 9.
The bid would total about $202 million for Exide's 10.1 million shares. Exides also has about $220 million in outstanding debt.
Exide urged its shareholders to take no action on the tender offer until the board had reviewed the bid and made a recommendation.
When Danaher announced the offer, it said it owned about 397,000 Exide shares.
Danaher, based in Washington, manufactures hand tools, including the Craftsman line sold by Sears Roebuck and Co, and process and environmental controls.
The company recently acquired Acme-Cleveland Corp and Joslyn Corp in deals that began with hostile offers but were agreed to after the bids were increased.
Analysts said Danaher may attempt a repeat of this strategy with Exide by raising its bid.
A new offer would have to exceed $22 per share since Exide stock is trading at that level, the sources said. Danaher made an earlier $22-per-share bid for Exide but was spurned.
Before Danaher's $20-a-share offer was made public, Exide shares were trading in a range of $10-$13.
In addition to the tender offer, Danaher has begun a legal offensive against Exide's resistance, alleging in a lawsuit "breach of fiduciary duties," according to Delaware Chancery Court papers.
In Monday afternoon trade Exide shares were off 1/4 to 22 on Nasdaq and Danaher was up 1/16 to 50-5/8 on the New York Stock Exchange.
